title: M12: Make it real: ESP32-C3 microcontroller course
description: Intent: As the student, I want to run my programs on a real microcontroller, so that machine code, memory-mapped I/O and loops become things I can see and touch. Why feasible: the ESP32-C3 core is RISC-V RV32IMC, our lesson ISA is RV32IM (the C compressed extension is off in lessons), so instructions transfer exactly. Classic ESP32, S2 and S3 are Xtensa (a different ISA) and are out of scope. Includes: a virtual ESP32-C3 dev board in the emulator (memory-mapped GPIO/LED, timer, UART at the real register addresses), a C3 memory map and linker script, a bare-metal firmware image path (startup code with watchdogs disabled, image format), optional flashing from the browser with esptool-js over Web Serial (Chrome or Edge), a Make-it-real course (blink, button, delays by counting steps, serial output), and a lesson on 16-bit compressed instructions. Hardware is optional: everything works on the virtual board first. Sequenced after the lesson player (M11).
